messages.subject: Re: Mplus not available (Mac)
messages.body_plain:
Hi there, Anja,

Do you have Mplus installed on the machine? For example, on my Mac, it's installed here: /Applications/Mplus. You won't be able to use MplusAutomation without this. If you have it installed in a non-standard location, you'll need pass the path to Mplus using the Mplus_command argument of readModels.

Hope this helps,
Michael

messages.body_plain:
Hi there, Andy,

As far as I know, there is no problem with reading outputs from models using multiple imputation. The error you mention suggests a problem identifying .out files in the folder you specified for readModels. If you send the exact R code and example .out files, we may be able to give you more specific feedback.

Michael

messages.subject: Re: Mplus not available (Mac)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Michael,

thanks for your reply!
Yes, Mplus is directly installed on the machine. For whatever reason, mplusAvailable() still tells me that its not, but it works now - I am able to run models through R.
I had some issues with the line breaks in my original input files, but after creating them directly with createModels and a template file, it worked fine now.
On my first try, I copied a displayed terminal command to my terminal directly and had to grant the terminal access rights to my files - maybe that is interesting for someone else as well.
In short: It works now, but I don't know why.

Cheers
Anja

messages.subject: Question on the estimated item probability to draw a profile plot
messages.subject_clean: Question on the estimated item probability to draw a profile plot
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am new to this MplusAutomation package, and it has been tremendously helpful.
I am trying to follow Figure 1 and code listing 2 in the article "MplusAutomation: An R Package for Facilitating Large-Scale Latent Variable Analyses in Mplus <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6075832/>" to draw profile plots.

If I understood correctly, the y axis of Figure 1 represents percentages of every value 1 versus value 0 in each of the categorical values. My question is what happens if I follow the code and draw plots using categorical data which has more than two categories. For example, in my data, some categorical variables have up to 4 categories. In this case, if I throw my data into the code, I get a profile plot that looks very similar to Figure 1, but I have no idea how to interpret this. Could anyone help me? If this plot/code is not the best way to compare different classes with categorical variables which are not binary, could anyone point me in the right direction? Thanks a lot!

Best,
Heeryung
